big_idea: People act with far more conviction on ideas they believe they discovered themselves than on ideas pitched at them. Instead of pushing a proposal, the skilled persuader engineers the conversation so the other person arrives at your idea on their own.

tool.label: The inception method
tool.text: A five-part sequence: Status Tip-Off, establishing yourself as a peer; Flash Roll, a burst of confident technical fluency; Pre-Wired Ideas, tapping existing beliefs; Plain Vanilla, framing the new idea as mostly familiar; and the Buyer's Formula, a structured walkthrough that lets the buyer discover your solution.
tool.note: Klaff, also author of Pitch Anything, built this as an extension of his earlier status and frame-based pitching work, aimed at high-stakes sales and negotiation.

ideas.title: Status tip-off
ideas.text: Quickly signal peer-level credibility through industry language and recent relevant work so people listen instead of resisting.

ideas.title: Flash roll
ideas.text: A rapid, confident, jargon-fluent explanation of a technical problem or solution that establishes expertise without over-explaining.

ideas.title: Pre-wired ideas
ideas.text: Trigger existing psychological drivers, like threat, reward, or fairness, so your pitch lands on beliefs the listener already holds.

ideas.title: Plain vanilla
ideas.text: Present an innovative idea as the same, except for one key difference, to lower resistance to change.

ideas.title: Strategic pessimism
ideas.text: Name your proposal's flaws yourself before the other person can, which builds credibility through apparent objectivity.

ideas.title: The buyer's formula
ideas.text: A structured sequence of failure modes and options that leads the listener to your preferred conclusion while feeling it was their own choice.

try_it: Before your next pitch or ask, script a 30-second status tip-off line establishing yourself as a peer, not a vendor.
Practice a 60-second flash roll explaining part of your work with zero hedging language.
Identify one real weakness in your own proposal and plan to name it yourself before someone else does.
Reframe one idea you want approved as just like X, with one difference, instead of presenting it as entirely new.
best_for: Entrepreneurs pitching investors or big deals
less_useful: Readers uneasy with overtly engineered persuasion tactics
Everyday, low-stakes conversations, since the framework is built for high-stakes sales

related.why: The same author's original frame-control system this book builds on
